title: 第十七章 黑市第十八章
slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌

苏尘是在院子门口遇见青萝的。
那天早上他起得比平时早了一些。深秋的清晨，天刚蒙蒙亮，院子里还笼着一层薄薄的雾气，石板地上覆着一层细密的白霜。他洗漱完推开院门，一眼就看见青萝从回廊那头走过来——换了一身干净的衣裳，不是平时在府里干活时穿的那件灰布褂子，而是一件深蓝色的半新短袄，头发也重新梳过了，利利落落地扎了个马尾。胳膊底下夹着一个青布挎袋，鼓鼓囊囊的，像是装了不少东西。
苏尘看了她一眼。
青萝也看见了他，脚步顿了一下，快步走过来，先开了口：
“世子今天起得早。“
“嗯。“苏尘的目光落在她胳膊底下的挎袋上，“要出门？“
“去蒙训院。“青萝说，语气很平常，像是在说一件再普通不过的事，“今天开课的日子，您忘了？“
苏尘没有忘。他只是没想起来今天是几号。蒙训院每旬开课五日、休息五日，轮到开课的日子，城里满了十五岁的少年男女就要去报到。青萝今年十六了，按理说已经去了一年多——但朝廷的规定是：十五岁入学，至少学满两年方可结业。她现在还是“在学“的状态。
朝廷设蒙训院，各州都有。年满十五岁、没有加入门派的少年，不论男女，一律必须入学。文的一边，教识字、算数、朝廷律法的基础；武的一边，教基础修炼功法、体能操练、简单的兵器使用。不教深的东西——两年时间不够教深的。它的目的很朴素：让每一个到了年纪的人至少能认几个字、会算简单的账、练一点粗浅的功夫防身。
在朔州这种边塞地方，蒙训院的武训比例要比内地高得多。毕竟北边就是寒渊，说不定哪一天战事吃紧，这些受过基础训练的年轻人就能直接补进后备军里。苏烈手底下不少兵，就是从朔州蒙训院出来的。苏尘有时候会想，朝廷设这个制度，说到底还是为了打仗准备的——文的部分只是顺带，武的部分才是根本。
“什么时候回来？“他问。
“申时前后吧。“青萝想了想，“上午是武课，下午是文课。要是武课拖堂了可能晚一些。“
苏尘点了点头。
青萝又看了他一眼。她张了张嘴，大概是想问他今天会不会出门、要不要她提前回来准备晚饭什么的——但嘴张了一下又闭上了。大概是想到苏尘一向不喜欢被人管着行踪，就没有多问，只是说了一句“那我走了“，就转身沿着回廊往外走了。
她走了几步，又回过头来补了一句：“厨房里有粥，早上刚熬的，您别忘了吃。“
说完这句她才真的走了。脚步声在清晨的院子里渐渐远去，拐过院门，消失在那头的薄雾里。
苏尘站在院子门口，看着那扇院门安静了片刻。
他吃了粥。
青萝熬的白粥，米粒已经煮得烂开，稠稠的，上面浮着一层薄薄的米油。配了一碟腌萝卜，切得细细的，拌了芝麻油和醋。他坐在厨房的小桌前慢慢地喝完了一碗，把碗洗干净扣在碗架上，然后出了门。

他没有往王府大门的方向走，而是穿过两条巷子，拐进了东市那条街。
清晨的东市比他想象中要热闹一些。卖早点的摊子已经支了起来，冒着白茫茫的蒸汽，混着面饼的焦香和油锅的滋滋声。几个早起赶集的农人挑着担子从城门口进来，箩筐里装着还带着露水的青菜，在石板路上留下一串湿漉漉的脚印。街角的茶水摊已经坐了人，几个穿着短打的汉子端着粗瓷碗蹲在路边喝热茶，一边喝一边有一搭没一搭地聊着天。一个半大的孩子蹲在杂货铺门口啃烧饼，一边啃一边拿眼睛瞟路过的人，大概是家里的伙计，等着掌柜开门好上工。
老周的算命摊也已经支起来了。
还是那张简陋的木桌、那块半旧的黑布，几支竹签插在筒里，旁边的地上放着一块写着“测字算命“的木牌，字迹被雨水冲刷得有些模糊了。老周坐在摊位后面，手里捧着一个粗瓷碗正在喝粥。他喝粥的样子很慢，不急不躁的，一碗粥能喝上半天。
看见苏尘走过来，他放下碗，拿袖子擦了擦嘴。
“少主今天来得早。“
“嗯。“苏尘在摊位前面的小板凳上坐下来。板凳只有一尺来高，他坐上去之后视线正好和老周的桌面齐平。他伸手进袖子里摸了摸，摸出一枚玄铢，放在桌上，“想托先生办件事。“
老周看了眼那枚玄铢，没有急着收。他先端起粥碗，把碗底最后一口喝干净了，在手里转了一圈，才不紧不慢地问：
“少主请说。“
“想去一趟城西。“
老周的目光在他脸上停了一瞬。那个停顿很短，但苏尘注意到了。然后老周点了点头，伸出两根手指，把那枚玄铢从桌面上夹起来，收进了袖子里。
城西有什么，他们两个心里都清楚。
黑市。
苏尘第一次知道城西地下有黑市，是一年前的事。
那时候他刚踏入淬体境不久。下品下的修为，修炼九境里最低的那一阶。丹田里那缕气感刚刚稳定下来，能完整地走完一个小周天而不在中途断掉。他开始琢磨着怎么把修为往上提一提——淬体境只是起步，后面还有凝元境、开脉境，越往上走越难。纳气法的效率摆在那里，想要加快速度，就需要一些辅助的东西。温养经脉的药散、帮助凝气的药草、提升运气效率的材料——这些东西，在皇城天邑的大药铺里不算难买，但在朔州这种边塞地方，正经药铺里根本进不到货。一来，这里的药铺多是进一些跌打损伤的药，辅助修炼类很少进，二来，太远了，运过来不划算，也没有那么多人买。想买，就只能去黑市。
他跟老周打听了一回。
老周当时正在整理他那几根竹签，听见苏尘的话，手上的动作没停。他沉默了一会儿，然后压低声音说了一句：
“城西地下有地方卖这些东西。但少主您一个人去不合适。“

Su Chen met Qing Luo at the gate of the courtyard.
He got up earlier than usual that morning. In the early morning of late autumn, it was just dawning. There was still a thin layer of mist hanging over the yard, and the stone floor was covered with a layer of fine white frost. After washing, he pushed open the courtyard door and saw Qing Luo coming from the other end of the corridor at a glance - she had changed into clean clothes, not the gray cloth gown she usually wore when working in the house, but a dark blue used short coat. Her hair had also been combed again and neatly tied into a ponytail. There was a green cloth satchel under his arm. It was bulging, as if it contained a lot of things.
Su Chen glanced at her.
Qingluo also saw him, paused for a moment, walked over quickly, and spoke first:
"Your Majesty got up early today."
"Yes." Su Chen's eyes fell on the satchel under her arm, "Want to go out?"
"Go to the Mentoring Academy." Qingluo said, her tone was very normal, as if she was talking about an ordinary thing, "Have you forgotten the day when classes start today?"
Su Chen has not forgotten. He just didn't remember what day it was. The Mentoring Academy opens for five days and rests for five days every ten days. When it is the day when classes start, all the young men and women in the city who are over fifteen years old have to report. Qingluo is sixteen this year, and it stands to reason that she has been there for more than a year - but the court's regulations are: she enters school at the age of fifteen and must study for at least two years before she can graduate. She is still in a "learning" state.
The imperial court established a training academy for men and women in every state. Young men and women who are over fifteen years old and have not joined a sect must enroll in school. The literary side teaches literacy, arithmetic, and the basics of court laws; the martial arts side teaches basic exercises, physical training, and the use of simple weapons. Don’t teach in-depth things—two years is not enough to teach in-depth things. Its purpose is very simple: to enable everyone of old age to at least recognize a few words, calculate simple accounts, and practice some superficial kung fu for self-defense.
In frontier places like Shuozhou, the proportion of martial arts training in the Meng Training Academy is much higher than in the mainland. After all, Hanyuan is to the north. Maybe one day when the war becomes serious, these young people who have received basic training can directly join the reserve army. Many of Su Lie's soldiers came from Shuozhou Meng Training Academy. Su Chen sometimes thought that the imperial court set up this system in the final analysis to prepare for war - the literary part was just incidental, but the military part was fundamental.
"When will you come back?" he asked.
"About Shenshi." Qingluo thought for a while, "There is martial arts class in the morning and literature class in the afternoon. If the martial arts class is delayed, it may be later."
Su Chen nodded.
Qingluo looked at him again. She opened her mouth, probably wanting to ask him if he would go out today and if he wanted her to come back early to prepare dinner or something - but she opened her mouth and closed it again. Probably because he thought that Su Chen didn't like having his whereabouts monitored, he didn't ask any more questions. He just said, "Then I'll go," and turned around and walked out along the corridor.
She walked a few steps, then turned back and added: "There is porridge in the kitchen. It was just cooked this morning. Don't forget to eat it."
After saying this, she really left. The footsteps gradually faded away in the early morning courtyard, turned around the courtyard gate, and disappeared into the mist at the other end.
Su Chen stood at the door of the courtyard and looked at the door for a moment of silence.
He ate porridge.
White porridge made with green radish, the rice grains have been boiled to a pulp, and it is thick with a thin layer of rice oil floating on it. It comes with a plate of pickled radish, finely chopped and mixed with sesame oil and vinegar. He sat at the small kitchen table and drank a bowl slowly, washed the bowl and put it on the dish rack, and then went out.
He did not walk towards the palace gate, but walked through two alleys and turned into the street of Dongshi.
The East Market in the early morning was busier than he imagined. The stall selling breakfast had already been set up, and white steam was rising, mixed with the aroma of burning bread and the sizzling sound of oil pan. A few farmers who got up early to go to the market came in from the city gate with their burdens, carrying baskets still covered with dew.The watery vegetables left a series of wet footprints on the stone road. The tea stall on the street corner was already occupied. Several men in short jackets were squatting on the roadside with thick porcelain bowls, drinking hot tea, and chatting away while drinking. A half-year-old child was squatting at the door of the grocery store, eating sesame seed cakes. While chewing, he glanced at the people passing by. They were probably the clerks at home, waiting for the shopkeeper to open the door and start work.
Lao Zhou's fortune-telling stall has also been set up.
It was still the simple wooden table, the half-old black cloth, and a few bamboo sticks inserted into the tube. Next to it was a wooden sign with the words "Calculation and Fortune Telling" on the ground. The writing was washed away by the rain and was a little blurry. Lao Zhou was sitting behind the stall, drinking porridge from a coarse porcelain bowl in his hand. He drank the porridge very slowly and without any rush. He could drink a bowl of porridge for half a day.
Seeing Su Chen coming over, he put down the bowl and wiped his mouth with his sleeve.
"Young Master came early today."
"Yeah." Su Chen sat down on the small bench in front of the stall. The bench was only about a foot high, and when he sat on it, his eyes were exactly level with Lao Zhou's desktop. He reached into his sleeve and touched it, took out a mysterious baht and put it on the table, "I want to ask Mr. to do something."
Lao Zhou glanced at the Xuan Baht and was not in a hurry to accept it. He picked up the porridge bowl first, drank the last sip from the bottom of the bowl, turned it around in his hand, and then asked calmly:
"Young Master, please speak."
"I want to go to the west of the city."
Lao Zhou's eyes stopped on his face for a moment. The pause was short, but Su Chen noticed it. Then Lao Zhou nodded, stretched out two fingers, picked up the Xuan Baht from the table, and put it into his sleeve.
They both knew what was in the west of the city.
black market.
It was a year ago that Su Chen first learned that there was a black market underground in the west of the city.
At that time, he had just entered the Body Tempering Realm. A low-level cultivation is the lowest level among the nine realms of cultivation. The qi feeling in the Dantian has just stabilized, and it can complete a small week without breaking in the middle. He began to think about how to improve his cultivation level - the Body Tempering Realm was just the beginning, and there would be the Yuan Condensing Realm and the Pulse Opening Realm later on, and the higher he went, the harder it would be. The efficiency of the Naqi method is there. If you want to speed up, you need some auxiliary things. Medicinal powders that warm the meridians, herbs that help condense qi, materials that improve luck efficiency - these things are not difficult to buy in large drug stores in the imperial city of Tianyi, but in frontier places like Shuozhou, they are simply not available in serious drug stores. Firstly, most of the pharmacies here sell medicines for bruises and injuries, but rarely for auxiliary exercises. Secondly, it’s too far away, so it’s not cost-effective to transport them here, and there aren’t that many people buying them. If you want to buy it, you have to go to the black market.
He asked Lao Zhou about it.
Lao Zhou was sorting out his bamboo sticks at the time, and when he heard Su Chen's words, he kept moving his hands. He was silent for a while, then lowered his voice and said:
"There is a place underground in the west of the city that sells these things. But it is not appropriate for you, young master, to go alone."
